title: Cleanup kernel registry and remove dead paths
author: Yuki Sato
summary: Removes legacy/unused kernel registry entries and simplifies fallback logic now that ADR-019 heuristics are the default path for H100/A100. Reduces registry surface area, makes fallback behavior deterministic and easier to reason about during perf canary, and deletes several dead feature-flag branches that were only used during earlier kernel experiments.
description: Context: After landing the FP8/INT8 auto-selection heuristics (ADR-019 / pr-19863) and shape guardrails (pr-19841, pr-19941), the kernel registry accumulated a number of stale entries and multi-hop fallbacks that are no longer reachable in production. This PR removes dead paths and simplifies the dispatch + fallback chain so the runtime has one clear decision point and one clear fallback per op. Changes: (1) Delete legacy registry keys for deprecated kernels (older CUTLASS INT8 matmul variants and pre-ADR fused attention entries) that are not referenced by any supported model profile. (2) Collapse fallback logic from (preferred -> alt -> legacy -> baseline) into (preferred -> baseline) with a single guardrail gate; the new heuristics already choose between FP8/INT8/baseline, so additional fallbacks were masking configuration errors and making perf canary harder to interpret. (3) Remove several unused flags and config aliases that only existed to support pre-sprint experiments; keep the currently documented flags (see pr-19903) unchanged. (4) Add lightweight validation: on startup, assert that registry entries referenced by model profiles exist; emit a single structured warning for unknown keys and fall back to baseline (rather than silently searching legacy aliases). (5) Minor cleanup: rename internal registry helpers for clarity and centralize default-kernel resolution in one file. Risk/compatibility: No behavior change for supported H100/A100 FP8/INT8 paths when flags and heuristics select supported kernels. For unknown/invalid registry keys, behavior becomes more explicit (warning + baseline) instead of implicit aliasing. This should improve canary debugging and reduce variance due to accidental kernel-mode drift. References: ADR-019; sprint epic ENG-7421; pr-19863 (heuristics), pr-19841 (INT8 guardrails), pr-19941 (hotfix disable FP8 for shape), pr-19934 (metrics tagging).
commits: refactor(kernel-registry): remove legacy aliases and unused entries
runtime(dispatch): simplify fallback chain to preferred -> baseline
runtime(validation): assert referenced registry keys exist; warn once on unknown
cleanup(flags): drop deprecated kernel experiment flags and config aliases
tests: update unit tests for deterministic fallback + registry validation
changed_areas: runtime/config/flags/* (removed deprecated flags; kept current names intact)
runtime/model_registry/* (updated references, removed legacy kernel keys)
test_plan: Unit: kernel registry/dispatch tests updated + extended to cover unknown-key warning + baseline fallback. CI smoke: quantized kernel correctness smoke bench (from pr-19926) run in presubmit. Manual: ran local microbench on H100 container image (CUDA pinned) for 3 representative shapes to confirm no regression and that selected kernel modes match pr-19863 output. Observability: verified that kernel-mode tagging remains unchanged (pr-19934) so perf-canary comparisons remain apples-to-apples.
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Can we confirm none of the deleted registry keys are referenced by any hosted model profiles or Dedicated overrides? If a customer has a stale override, what happens?

Yuki Sato (author): Confirmed via grep + model registry validation added in this PR. If a stale override exists, we now emit one structured warning at startup and fall back to baseline; previously it would silently alias to legacy keys, which made canary data ambiguous.
Noah Patel: Please ensure fallback is deterministic and does not depend on registry iteration order. Also, can we make the warning include the model + op + key for easier triage?
Yuki Sato (author): Done. Fallback resolution is now a single explicit path. Warning includes model_id, gpu_arch, op, requested_key, and resolved_key=baseline.
Sofia Ivanova: Any scheduler side-effects? We saw in the sprint that multi-hop fallbacks can change queueing patterns mid-run.
Yuki Sato (author): This should reduce that risk. We removed the secondary fallback hop that could switch kernels after a guardrail failure; now guardrail failure goes directly to baseline.
Grace Kim: Small nit: keep the public flag names unchanged (docs + runbook reference them).
Yuki Sato (author): Confirmed. Removed only deprecated experimental flags; current documented flags remain unchanged.
Marcus Reed: Looks good. Please add a short note in the internal runtime docs to avoid folks trying to use the removed aliases in ad-hoc benchmark configs.
Yuki Sato (author): Added a note to docs/internal/runtime-kernel-flags.md and referenced the new validation behavior.
rollout_notes: No rollout action required by itself. This reduces ambiguity during the ongoing FP8/INT8 perf canary by making fallback behavior explicit and stable. If we observe a spike in baseline fallback warnings in canary, treat as misconfiguration and triage per fp8/int8 regression playbook.
release_notes: Internal: Kernel registry cleanup. Removed legacy kernel keys/aliases; fallback is now preferred->baseline with explicit warnings for unknown keys. No change to current documented flag names.
